title: Classic to Wrath
editionLabel: World of Warcraft · Classic, The Burning Crusade, and Wrath of the Lich King
summary: Choose a story from the map, or play the completed stories in chronological order across Azeroth, Outland, and Northrend.
opening: Azeroth's northern continents, the broken world of Outland, and the frozen reaches of Northrend frame a new kind of journey: each story stands on its own, while the whole tour follows the great campaigns in turn.
mapAlt: An original interpretive world atlas: Kalimdor to the west, the Eastern Kingdoms to the east, Northrend in the north, and Outland as a separate shattered landmass at the lower right, with varied marsh, forest, volcanic, and crystal terrain.
mapInterpretationNote: Original AI-generated overview art for tour navigation, not an official World of Warcraft map or a surveyed geographic reconstruction. Story markers use illustration layout positions only; they are not atlas coordinates or exact zone locations. Outland is a separate worldspace and is shown detached from Azeroth; no travel route is implied. Intended visual reference: the Wrath of the Lich King world presentation, before Cataclysm changed Azeroth.
chronologyNote: Play-all order is an editorial expansion-era sequence: Classic (Onyxia, Scepter, Dungeon Set 2, the Fallen Hero, Tirion and Taelan, Darrowshire, then the Defias and the Unsent Letter, followed by the Scythe of Elune investigations), The Burning Crusade (Karazhan, Akama and the Black Temple, the Outland Cipher, then The Missing Diplomat’s patch 2.3 continuation), and Wrath (Wrathgate followed by Quel’Delar). The Scythe of Elune entries combine Velinde’s original quest chain with Jitters’s separate Duskwood testimony as an editorially linked research story, not a prerequisite chain; its single map marker is a tour-layout anchor. The Missing Diplomat begins with a distinct original Classic chain and is placed here because its final playable segment was added in patch 2.3; this ordering does not claim a cross-story quest dependency or a precise date. The Classic ordering is a navigational sequence and does not claim canonical relative dates or causal links across separate stories. Darrowshire’s Third War fall is a labeled flashback; its Classic investigation and constrained battle replay remain distinct. The Annals’ Second War date is disputed. The Defias visitor “Maelik” remains unresolved until Shaw’s report, and the Stormwind report handoff is not connected to Onyxia. Other branch, faction and flashback caveats remain as recorded in each story. Ras Frostwhisper is placed after Yeh’kinya and before the Burning Crusade stories as an editorial Classic-era playlist position; its exact in-world date and any causal link to those stories are unknown.
